record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: For beauty quarks in the QGP, whose diffusion estimates place the hydrodynamization time scale near the QGP lifetime while recent lattice-QCD calculations suggest possible partial hydrodynamization, what is the actual degree of beauty-quark participation in collective medium dynamics, especially at low transverse momentum, and how can future Run 3 measurements of RAA and anisotropic-flow observables constrain QGP parameters?

evidence.quote: Regarding beauty quarks, Ds estimates predict the hydrodynamization time-scale might be of the order of the typical lifetime of the QGP and might not fulfill the conditions for fluid-dynamic applicability. However, the most recent lQCD calculations suggest a possible partial hydrodynamization of beauty quarks.

From the experimental side, several measurements of open and hidden beauty have been published, however, the precision achieved does not yet allow us to draw firm conclusions on their dynamic in the QGP.
The non-prompt v3 coefficient results have large statistical uncertainties so that neither the pT nor the centrality dependence can be determined.

However, results of RAA and v2 are still not conclusive when the physics of low pT beauty quark tries to be addressed, making future Run 3 measurements extremely important to further address the dynamic of the beauty quark and to further constrain QGP parameters using heavy quarks as probes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider beauty quarks (b-quarks, mass ≈ 4.18 GeV) produced in heavy-ion collisions and propagating through a deconfined quark–gluon plasma (QGP). Model their interaction with the medium as a stochastic process characterized by a spatial diffusion coefficient D_s (or equivalently a momentum diffusion coefficient κ), so that the thermalization/hydrodynamization time scale is τ_Q ∼ (M/T) · D_s, where M is the heavy-quark mass and T the medium temperature. Because M_b ≫ T, simple Brownian-motion estimates suggest τ_Q for beauty is comparable to the typical QGP lifetime (∼ 5–10 fm/c), while recent nonperturbative (lattice-QCD) determinations of κ at temperatures relevant to the QGP yield smaller D_s, suggesting at least partial hydrodynamization is possible within the medium lifetime.

(a) Determine quantitatively to what extent beauty quarks participate in the collective dynamics of the QGP — in particular, characterize, as a function of transverse momentum p_T (with emphasis on the low-p_T region p_T ≲ M_b), the magnitude of the nuclear modification factor
   R_AA(p_T) = (1/⟨N_coll⟩) · (dN_AA/dp_T)/(dN_pp/dp_T)
for non-prompt (beauty-decay) D and J/ψ mesons and B mesons, and of the anisotropic-flow Fourier coefficients
   v_n(p_T) = ⟨cos[n(φ − Ψ_n)]⟩, n = 2, 3,
of the same beauty-hadron observables.

(b) Given a set of such measurements (with the statistical and systematic precision expected from LHC Run 3 Pb–Pb data sets), determine the precision with which one can extract the temperature-dependent spatial diffusion coefficient 2πT·D_s(T) of beauty quarks in the QGP, and assess whether the data can discriminate between models in which beauty quarks fully hydrodynamize, partially hydrodynamize, or remain out of equilibrium throughout the medium evolution.
artifact.status_search_result: Current literature (2023–2025) confirms the question is unresolved. Recent lattice-QCD computations of the heavy-quark momentum diffusion coefficient indicate possible partial hydrodynamization of beauty quarks, but precision experimental constraints on beauty R_AA and v_n at low p_T are not yet available; the community is awaiting LHC Run 3 measurements to constrain QGP transport parameters from beauty observables.

status_evidence.title: Heavy Quark Diffusion from 2+1 Flavor Lattice QCD with 320 MeV Pion Mass
status_evidence.snippet: For 195 MeV < T < 352 MeV, the heavy-quark spatial diffusion coefficient is significantly smaller than previous estimates, implying fast hydrodynamization of heavy quarks in the QGP.
status_evidence.claim: Recent lattice QCD finds smaller D_s, supporting (partial) hydrodynamization of heavy quarks including beauty.

status_evidence.title: Heavy quark momentum diffusion coefficient during hydrodynamization via effective kinetic theory
status_evidence.snippet: Heavy quark momentum diffusion coefficient computed via QCD effective kinetic theory through bottom-up thermalization; nonthermal κ matches thermal value within 30%.
status_evidence.claim: Pre-equilibrium and partial hydrodynamization effects for heavy quarks remain an active research area.

status_evidence.title: Investigating charm-quark dynamics in the QGP via the charm-hadron elliptic flow in Pb–Pb collisions with ALICE
status_evidence.snippet: Recent Run 3 measurements of prompt and non-prompt charm-hadron v2 at √s_NN = 5.36 TeV.
status_evidence.claim: Run 3 measurements relevant to constraining heavy-quark transport are only beginning to appear.
